Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment
In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 05.04.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.250/2014 by the MACT and I Additional Senior Civil Judge, Kolar ('the Tribunal' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 27.05.2013, while the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-43-K- 2224 at about 11.00 a.m. near Koleman Factory Private Limited on Kolar-Bengaluru NH-4, a car bearing registration No.HR-51-W-0347 which was going ahead of the petitioner's motorcycle, all of a sudden stopped on the road due to which NC: 2024:KHC:32217 the petitioner hit on the hind portion of the car and sustained injuries and treated in hospital.

Being an electrician,
he suffered permanent disability.
The petitioner spent money towards treatment and incidental expenses.
The petitioner approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence and on hearing both the parties, by the impugned judgment and award assessed the following compensation and attributed equal contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.

1. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 20,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.28,100/-
3. Incidental charges Rs.1,000/-

4. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.6,000/-
5. Loss of amenities Rs.10,000/-
6. Conveyance Rs.500/-
Total Rs.65,600/-
The award of the Tribunal is satisfied by the Insurance Company.
Pleading inadequacy of compensation and questioning the attribution of contributory negligence against him, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard Sri Gopal Krishna N, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri L. Sreekanta Rao, learned counsel for respondent No.2 Insurance Company.
NC: 2024:KHC:32217 5.

It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the car while going ahead, without giving any indication, all of a sudden stopped, facilitating the petitioner to hit on the back side of the car.
There is no contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.

Without considering this aspect,
the Tribunal attributed 50% contributory negligence against the petitioner.
The petitioner has suffered dislocation of left hip with foot drop.
The medical evidence is placed by P.W.1 to explain 17.3% whole body disability.
The Tribunal did not consider the same and not awarded the compensation towards future loss of income.
The compensation awarded under different heads is inadequate and sought for enhancement.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that the car was going ahead of the motorcycle.
It is the duty on the part of the petitioner being a rider to be careful when a car is going ahead.
Without following the road rules and maintaining the minimum distance, he had gone and hit against the car.
The Tribunal is not proper to attribute 50% of contributory negligence.
Complete negligence has to be attributed against the NC: 2024:KHC:32217 petitioner.
Post treatment, the petitioner became normal and he is earning and the compensation is proportionate to the nature of injuries and it is not a case for enhancement.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for both the parties and perused the material on record.
8. The material on record shows that there was an accident involving the car and motorcycle on 27.05.2013.
The evidence point out that the car had stopped on the road all of a sudden and the petitioner hit on the back side of the car.
No doubt, the petitioner ought to have been careful in riding the motorcycle.
The evidence suggest that the car stopped on the road all of a sudden without giving signal.
Therefore, the Tribunal considered equal contributory negligence, but the evidence suggest that the negligence on the part of the driver of the car at 60% and that of the petitioner at 40%.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for 60% of the compensation.

sentences.text: P.W.2 is the treated doctor and his evidence shows dislocation of left hip with foot drop and the petitioner has NC: 2024:KHC:32217 suffered static nerve injury.
According to the doctor, the petitioner has suffered 36.9% of limb disability and 17.3% of whole body disability.

The Tribunal did not consider this aspect, as in the course of cross-examination, the petitioner has admitted that he has become normal after the treatment and now he is working with one Suresh and drawing salary.
The findings recorded by the Tribunal is proper.

10. The petitioner has sustained dislocation of left hip and certainly suffered pain and suffering and underwent ordeal of amenities and discomfort, spent money towards incidental charges and he will lose the income during the laid up period.
Hence, towards pain and suffering an amount of Rs.40,000/-, towards medical expenses an amount of Rs.28,100/-, towards incidental charges an amount of Rs.5,000/- is assessed.
11. The accident is of the year 2013.
The petitioner has not produced any evidence to show his income.
Even if he is treated as a person with no proof of income, in the year 2013, such person will earn not less than Rs.8,000/- per month.

Hence, his notional income is taken at Rs.8,000/- per NC:
2024:KHC:32217 month.
Towards loss of income during the laid up period for three months an amount of Rs.24,000/- (Rs.8,000/- x 3 months) and towards loss of amenities and discomfort an amount of Rs.40,000/- is assessed.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation as follows:
1. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 40,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.28,100/-
3. Incidental charges Rs.5,000/-
4. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.24,000/-
5. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs.40,000/-

Total Rs.1,37,100/-
 Less compensation Rs.65,600/-
 awarded by the Tribunal  Enhanced compensation Rs. 71,500/-
It is the just compensation the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.

12. In view of above discussion, appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
